steps.observation: Work on this for 30 seconds; do not stop early. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
Here are the principal differences between DNA and RNA:

1. Sugar backbone  
   • DNA contains deoxyribose (lacks one oxygen atom on the 2′ carbon)  
   • RNA contains ribose (has an –OH group on the 2′ carbon)

2. Nitrogenous bases  
   • DNA uses adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), and thymine (T)  
   • RNA uses A, G, C, and uracil (U) instead of thymine

3. Strandedness  
   • DNA is typically double-stranded, forming a stable double helix  
   • RNA is usually single-stranded and can fold into diverse 3D shapes

4. Function  
   • DNA stores and preserves genetic information long-term  
   • RNA conveys and helps execute genetic instructions (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA, regulatory RNAs, etc.)

5. Stability and location  
   • DNA is more chemically stable (favors long-term storage) and is found mainly in the nucleus (eukaryotes) or nucleoid (prokaryotes)  
   • RNA is less stable (more prone to hydrolysis), and exists in nucleus and cytoplasm (eukaryotes) or throughout the cell (prokaryotes)

Together, these differences enable DNA to serve as the “blueprint” of life, while RNA acts as the “messenger,” “assembler,” and regulator in gene expression and other cellular processes.
